title: HomeOps: a household agent for Alexa+

segments.narration: It's seven in the morning in a busy home. What's due today? What's running low? Are we still on budget? HomeOps is a self-hosted MCP server that lets Alexa+ answer all of it, and act on it, in one conversation.

segments.heading: One question, the whole morning
say: Alexa, what's going on at home today?
segments.narration: One question gets the whole morning: today's tasks, whose turn it is for chores, what's running low, and the budget, chained into a single tool call.

say: Alexa, what's going on at home today?
segments.expect: Alexa+ calls run_morning_briefing. HomeOps returns: 1 task due today (take out recycling), Sam is next up for chores, 2 items running low, spending on track.

segments.heading: Just say it
segments.narration: Nobody needs to know which tool does what. HomeOps sorts a plain sentence into the shopping list, a task, or an expense.

segments.expect: capture_note adds coffee to the shopping list, then logs $120 under groceries (Alexa+ may call add_expense directly for the second one, which is also fine).

segments.heading: Asks before it spends
segments.narration: Before it spends anything, HomeOps asks. Alexa+ puts a real confirmation in front of you, and nothing is ordered without a yes.

segments.expect: reorder_item sends an MCP elicitation: "Dog food has 0 on hand. Reorder it now?" After you confirm: "Reordered Dog food. It now shows 2 on hand once delivered."

segments.heading: Speaks up before problems happen
say: Is there anything I should know about?
segments.narration: And it speaks up before problems happen. That grocery run puts the week on pace to blow far past its budget, so HomeOps flags it now, not at the end of the week.

say: Is there anything I should know about?
segments.expect: get_proactive_alerts: groceries spent 120 of 150 in 1 day, on pace for ~840 (460% over); paper towels low with no reorder on record. The dog-food alert is gone because it was just reordered.

segments.narration: Under the hood, HomeOps runs on Amazon ECS Express Mode, deployed from AWS CloudShell with one command. When a client can't run its own model, it calls Claude on Amazon Bedrock through a least-privilege role.
Every tool is tested end to end against a real MCP client: forty-one checks, including the Bedrock path.
HomeOps. A household agent that asks before it spends, and speaks up before problems happen.
